definitions: The compound annual growth rate (CAGR) is the mean annual growth rate of an investment over a specified period longer than one year, calculated as if the investment had grown at this rate every year, compounded annually.
A business metric used to measure the average annual growth of something over a period of time longer than one year.
examples: The company's revenue showed a 10% CAGR over the last five years.
Investors often look at CAGR to understand the smoothed growth of an asset.
